response.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN c.state IS NULL OR TRIM(c.state) = '' THEN NULL ELSE c.state END AS state, COUNT(*) AS matched_records, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_college) AS share_of_all_records FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON c.college_id = pc.college_id GROUP BY CASE WHEN c.state IS NULL OR TRIM(c.state) = '' THEN NULL ELSE c.state END;

assumptions.assumption: College matching is an inner join on exact equality of college_id, so player_college rows with no matching college are dropped from the groups. college_id is assumed unique in college; otherwise the join would multiply counts.
A blank state is NULL, an empty string, or whitespace only; these are grouped together and reported as NULL. Other state values are reported as stored, without case or whitespace normalization.

The denominator is the count of all player_college rows, including those whose college is not found. The division uses REAL arithmetic to avoid integer truncation and is not rounded. The table is assumed to be non-empty.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat only NULL and the empty string as blank; whitespace-only states are kept as their own distinct state value.
alternatives.sql: SELECT COALESCE(c.state, '') AS state, COUNT(*) AS matched_records, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_college) AS share_of_all_records FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON c.college_id = pc.college_id GROUP BY COALESCE(c.state, '');
